claim: `cb.verify.route_tags` re-derives each sink's excerpt log from the current route tags and fails on divergence, converting the log's freshness guarantee from procedural to structural; it also enforces that every ref resolves to a real artifact and every tagged sink carries its log. Tag coverage (that every feeding paragraph was tagged) stays editorial and is lifted only to row granularity by a routing-ledger cross-check.

evidence.detail: Staged and grounded in the route-tagging proto-belief document as the structural backstop the F2 disposition demands: the verifier closes the forgotten-append and un-propagated-correction exposures for tags that exist, and is honest about the coverage axis it cannot mechanize.

Implemented as mix cb.verify.route_tags (lib/cb/route_tags.ex): five checks - wellformedness, ref resolution, sink logs, log fidelity (byte-level re-derivation match), ledger cross-check at warn level. Its first run reproduced audit finding F5 (transcript-format tagged but no log), fixed in the same commit.

Session thread retro-pair (cb:b507): the minting session's finalized thread persists at the cited document - the A2 enactment that built mix cb.verify.route_tags (whose first run reproduced audit F5 and whose derivation materialized the missing transcript-format log), minted the three route-tagging rows through clean preflights, and graduated the source document to beliefs/archive/ on the cb:b569 call, with council-mechanism held live.
